s.t: SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

As a member of the SpaceX Construction & Engineering team you will be directly responsible for translating engineering and production requirements into executable plans. You will also manage and update campus maps and individual building drawings as the needs of the business evolve.

You will work with a group of elite engineers across multiple disciplines to design, build, and activate infrastructure that will enable orbital launch capability for the largest rocket in the world. This position is based in Hawthorne, CA.

Mission Support Facilities Division provides the facilities and associated infrastructure, facilities management, and sustainment to support CBP mission support office operations.

As stewards of a large national portfolio of GSA-owned and CBP-owned infrastructure, MSF carefully balances resources to ensure the right facilities are planned and delivered at the right time to meet mission requirements.

The Enterprise Facilities Support (EFS)PMO is comprised of three branches - Facilities and Infrastructure Management, Housing, and Program Management.

These branches are responsible for the planning, development, and execution of facility projects, handling maintenance and repairs, and coordinating/evaluating Facility Condition Assessments for all mission support facilities outside of the National Capital Region, including CBP's portfolio of residential housing.

Basic Requirements: Degree: architecture; or related field that included 60 semester hours of course work in architecture or related disciplines of which at least (1) 30 semester hours were in architectural design, and (2) 6 semester hours were in each of the following: structural technology, properties of materials and methods of construction, and environmental control systems.

OR Combination of Education and Experience: College-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the arts and sciences underlying professional architecture, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the architectural principles, methods, and techniques and their applications to the design and construction or improvement of buildings.

The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by at least one of the following: Related Curriculum: Degree in architectural engineering may be accepted as satisfying in full the basic requirements, provided the completed course work in architectural engineering provided knowledge, skills, and abilities substantially equivalent to those provided in the courses specified in paragraph A.

The curriculum for a degree in either architecture or architectural engineering covers function, esthetics, site, structure, economics, mechanical-electrical, and other engineering problems related to the design and construction of buildings primarily (but not exclusively) intended to house human activities.

The courses required for a degree in architecture generally place emphasis upon planning, esthetics, and materials and methods of construction, while the courses for an architectural engineering degree place equal or greater weight on the technical engineering aspects such as structural systems, mechanical systems, and the properties of materials.

Because of this difference in emphasis, persons with degrees in architecture may have a preference for work assignments that offer greater opportunities for them to express their artistic and creative abilities.

As a result, they may be more concerned with planning and design aspects of architecture, and persons with degrees in architectural engineering may be more engaged in aspects emphasizing technical engineering considerations.

Experience: An applicant lacking a degree in architecture must have had l year of experience in an architect's office or in architectural work for each year short of graduation from a program of study in architecture. In the absence of college courses, 5 years of such experience is required.

This experience must have demonstrated that the applicant has acquired a thorough knowledge of the fundamental principles and theories of professional architecture.

As a result, they may be more concerned with planning and design aspects of architecture, and persons with degrees in architectural engineering may be more engaged in aspects emphasizing technical engineering considerations.

To be acceptable, the curriculum must: (1) be in a school of engineering with at least one curriculum accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET) as a professional engineering curriculum; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics.

OR Combination of education and experience: college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying professional engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering.

The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: Professional registration, Written Test, Specified academic courses and Related curriculum. Professional registration -- Current registration as a professional engineer by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico.

Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration.

For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions.

Written Test-- Evidence of having successfully passed the Engineer-in-Training (EIT) examination, or the written test required for professional registration, which is administered by the Boards of Engineering Examiners in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.

Applicants who have passed the EIT examination and have completed all the requirements for either (a) a bachelor's degree in engineering technology (BET) from an accredited college of university that included 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences, or (b) a BET from a program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET) may be rated eligible for certain engineering positions at GS-5.

Eligibility is limited to positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of the engineering technology program.

Because of the diversity in kind and quality of BET programs, graduates of other BET programs are required to complete at least 1 year of additional education or highly technical work experience of such nature as to provide reasonable assurance of the possession of the knowledge, skills, and abilities required for professional engineering competence.

The adequacy of this background must be demonstrated by passing the EIT examination. Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified in the basic requirements.

The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of a professional engineering curriculum.

Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering technology or in an appropriate professional field, e.g., physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.

Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions.

(The above examples of related curricula are not all-inclusive) SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Must have at least 1 year (12 months) of experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade.

You'll join Luno's Architecture team, a small group of architects who each own the architecture across Luno's business portfolios, alongside specialists in data and blockchain architecture. It's a close-knit community: architects review each other's work, share standards and patterns, and keep Luno's platform coherent as a whole.

You'll be embedded in the Payments & OTC portfolio, the teams that move money in and out of Luno: fiat payment and banking integrations across more than 40 countries, payment orchestration, settlement infrastructure, and the OTC desk that serves our largest customers.

The portfolio is backend-heavy and integration-rich, spanning banks, payment providers and partner platforms, but its products surface directly in Luno's consumer and institutional web and mobile apps, so the architecture runs the full stack, all in a regulated environment.

You own the system architecture of the portfolio. You work as a standing peer alongside its engineering and product leadership, accountable for architectural integrity across its systems: "is it designed right, and does it fit Luno?"

This is not a coding role; its value lies in altitude and breadth, holding the architectural view across many teams and systems at once. You work through design artefacts, review and influence rather than mandate. You'll still build the occasional proof of concept, and you stay close enough to the codebase to be credible across the stack, but delivery belongs to the teams.

· Own the architectural view of the portfolio: a clear, current map of its systems, contracts and domain models that teams actually use

· Author high-level designs for new capabilities, and review and sign off the technical designs teams produce, guiding through questions and evidence rather than verdicts

· Record consequential decisions and their rationale so they're made once and stay discoverable

· Partner deeply with product and engineering leadership: shape scope and sequencing early, and translate in both directions between product intent and architectural constraint

· Partner with commercial teams: solution architecture for bank, payment provider and partner integrations, and technical credibility in sales and vendor conversations

· Drive our payment orchestration and settlement architecture: shape how an orchestration layer works alongside dozens of existing provider integrations, set the patterns that make new payment integrations repeatable rather than bespoke, and guide how the OTC desk integrates with Luno's brokerage and liquidity infrastructure

· Guide the client-side architecture of the portfolio's payment experiences as our apps migrate onto a new Flutter-based mobile architecture, keeping payment flows coherent from tap to settlement

· Design for the regulated context: compliance, security and data protection are design inputs, not afterthoughts

· Champion AI adoption: use AI tooling in your own design work, help teams apply it well, and shape where AI-assisted capabilities belong in the products we build

· Connect the portfolio to Luno's wider architecture community: bring standards and golden paths in, carry friction back out, and keep your decisions coherent with the rest of the platform

· You've architected consumer-facing, high-scale distributed systems; your recent leverage has come from design, writing and influence rather than commits. Financial services experience is advantageous.

· You're comfortable this isn't a coding role: you can still build a proof of concept, and you read code well enough to understand a system across the stack, from clients to backend services and data

· You write and communicate exceptionally well, and bring structure to ambiguity

· You influence without authority, and know when to let a team diverge and simply document the trade-off

· You are experienced in backend architecture: you're fluent in the trade-offs of event-driven architecture, microservices, API and domain modelling, and at least one major cloud provider (ideally AWS)

· You've worked with payment systems: payment providers, orchestration, settlement and reconciliation, and the realities of integrating with banks and partners across many markets. OTC or trading systems experience is a plus.

· You're credible across web and mobile client architecture too, and can guide teams building rich client experiences on top of a complex backend (Flutter experience is a plus)

· Previous experience as a software engineer in a modern language, with strong product sense

· You've worked in regulated markets, or design with compliance, security and data protection as first-class constraints

· You use AI tools as a working instrument, with sound judgment about their limits, and you're excited to help an organisation adopt them well

· You can translate architecture for product, compliance, commercial and executive audiences, including across the table from a bank, partner or customer's technical team

BASIC REQUIREMENT: Degree: architecture; or related field that included 60 semester hours of course work in architecture or related disciplines of which at least (1) 30 semester hours were in architectural design, and (2) 6 semester hours were in each of the following: structural technology, properties of materials and methods of construction, and environmental control systems. -OR- Combination of Education and Experience: college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the arts and sciences underlying professional architecture, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the architectural principles, methods, and techniques and their applications to the design and construction or improvement of buildings.

The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by at least one of the following: Related Curriculum: Degree in architectural engineering may be accepted as satisfying in full the basic requirements, provided the completed course work in architectural engineering provided knowledge, skills, and abilities substantially equivalent to those provided in the courses specified in paragraph A.

The curriculum for a degree in either architecture or architectural engineering covers function, esthetics, site, structure, economics, mechanical-electrical, and other engineering problems related to the design and construction of buildings primarily (but not exclusively) intended to house human activities.

The courses required for a degree in architecture generally place emphasis upon planning, esthetics, and materials and methods of construction, while the courses for an architectural engineering degree place equal or greater weight on the technical engineering aspects such as structural systems, mechanical systems, and the properties of materials.

Because of this difference in emphasis, persons with degrees in architecture may have a preference for work assignments that offer greater opportunities for them to express their artistic and creative abilities.

As a result, they may be more concerned with planning and design aspects of architecture, and persons with degrees in architectural engineering may be more engaged in aspects emphasizing technical engineering considerations.

Experience: An applicant lacking a degree in architecture must have had l year of experience in an architect's office or in architectural work for each year short of graduation from a program of study in architecture. In the absence of college courses, 5 years of such experience is required.

This experience must have demonstrated that the applicant has acquired a thorough knowledge of the fundamental principles and theories of professional architecture. -AND- FOR THE GS-13 LEVEL: Applicants must have one year of specialized experience (equivalent to the GS-12 level) that may have been obtained in the private or public (local, county, state, Federal) sectors which demonstrates: (1) Preparing architectural/engineering designs, specifications, and estimates; (2) Reviewing and providing technical comments on architectural/engineering designs, specifications, and estimates; (3) Briefing leadership on the status, progress, and issues surrounding architectural projects; (4) Analyzing, interpreting, and compiling quantitative data and construction documents to support planning, reporting, and decision-making; (5) Producing architectural drawings that incorporate applicable design standards and requirements.

Note: There is no education substitution for this grade level. TRANSCRIPTS are required: This position requires specific coursework or a degree in a specific field to be basically qualified. This education must have been successfully completed and obtained from an accredited school, college, or university.

To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics.

OR Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering.

The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT)1, or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico.

Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration.

For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions.

Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE)2 examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.

Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A.

The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A.

Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.

Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. (The above examples of related curricula are not all inclusive.)

Job Description
We are looking for a highly experienced DevSecOps Architect to lead enterprise DevSecOps and platform engineering strategy across cloud-native engineering teams. This role owns the design, governance, and evolution of secure, scalable, reusable platform capabilities that enable standardized self-service delivery, improve developer productivity, and accelerate high-quality software releases.
The DevSecOps Architect will provide technical leadership across CI/CD, GitOps, cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes platforms, security integration, observability, compliance automation, and AI-augmented engineering practices. The role requires strong architectural thinking, hands-on engineering depth, excellent communication skills, stakeholder influence, and the ability to translate complex platform and security needs into practical, business-aligned engineering solutions.

Bachelors or master’s in engineering, MCA, M.Sc. in Computer Science, IT
Relevant certifications in cloud, DevSecOps, Kubernetes, security, architecture, or platform engineering are preferred.

15+ years of IT experience with strong expertise in DevSecOps, platform engineering, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD automation, release engineering, security integration, observability, and enterprise-scale engineering enablement.

Architect and govern enterprise DevSecOps and platform engineering strategy, including scalable platforms, reusable frameworks, golden paths, self-service enablement, and standardized developer workflows.
Design and lead CI/CD ecosystems using GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines to improve release reliability, traceability, and consistency.
Drive automation across the software delivery lifecycle, including workflow automation, reusable tool chains, policy-as-code, automated controls, and DevSecOps metrics.
Architect cloud-native infrastructure using Terraform, Kubernetes, EKS, Helm, Argo CD, Karpenter, Docker, and GitOps operating models.
Integrate security and compliance into engineering platforms using tools and practices such as Fortify, GitHub Advanced Security, Secret Scanning, Black Duck, Dependabot, Kyverno, Cilium, RBAC, least privilege access, and secure SDLC controls.
Define observability and reliability practices using Prometheus, Grafana, Tempo, Loki, alerting, incident response, root cause analysis, SRE practices, and platform health monitoring.
Provide architectural guidance and enablement to R&D, platform, security, and engineering teams through mentoring, governance, standards definition, documentation, and stakeholder collaboration.

Deep expertise in DevSecOps, platform engineering, cloud-native architecture, CI/CD automation, GitOps, release engineering, security integration, and operational excellence.
Strong scripting and automation skills using Python, Shell scripting, PowerShell, and workflow automation approaches.

About Showpad
Showpad is the leader in revenue effectiveness, helping organizations in complex, field-driven industries turn strategy into execution and execution into measurable growth. Purpose-built for industrial organizations such as those in manufacturing, consumer packaged goods, and medical device companies, Showpad’s AI-native platform unifies content management, sales readiness, buyer engagement, and revenue intelligence into a single system of execution.
Powered by GenieAI and grounded in trusted first-party data, Showpad enables revenue teams to automate workflows, scale winning behaviors, and reclaim lost revenue across every customer interaction. More than 2,000 global organizations rely on Showpad to drive consistent, high-impact performance in the field.
Built for effectiveness and recognized for excellence, Showpad is consistently named a Leader by Gartner, Forrester, IDC, and Aragon, and backed by 2,500+ five-star reviews on G2 and Gartner Peer Insights.

As Chief Architect you set and steward the architectural direction of Showpad's entire product portfolio. You are the CTO's principal technical partner: the person who defines the target-state architecture, sequences the runway to get there, holds the bar on technical quality, and makes the economics of AI and cloud a first-class design consideration rather than an after-the-fact surprise.
The role is deeply technical and deeply cross-functional. You will spend your time in design reviews and equally in rooms with Product, GTM, customers, the executive leadership team and the board — and you will be expected to be credible and additive in all of them.

Portfolio architecture. Own and lead the overall architectural direction across multiple products, defining the target-state platform architecture and the pragmatic path from where each product is today.
Architecture Review Board. Chair and run the ARB — establishing standards, reference architectures, decision records and review cadence, and making it a forum engineers actively bring work to rather than a gate they route around.
Architecture and design runways. Embed directly in the development process where complex deliverables require an architecture or design runway ahead of execution, and stay engaged through delivery rather than handing off a document.
Customer engagement. Represent Showpad's technology to customers and prospects — architecture, security and AI deep dives, plus the product and commercial context that makes them land with an economic buyer.
Technology transformation. Lead modernization of complex, dated products in the portfolio: assess, sequence, de-risk and drive multi-year transformation without stalling the roadmap.
Staffing and operating models. Recommend staffing and sourcing models to the CTO that are efficient on both cost and execution — including global team topology, build/buy decisions and skill mix.
AI and cloud economics. Establish the practices, guardrails and observability that keep AI inference, AI-assisted development and cloud operating costs predictable and defensible as we scale.
Role model. Set the standard for business-aware technical excellence — engineering judgment that is rigorous about quality and equally rigorous about cost, time-to-value and customer outcome.

Experience
15+ years of industry experience, with substantial depth in B2B SaaS.
Has led architecture and development for large-scale enterprise products — multi-tenant, security- and compliance-sensitive, with demanding enterprise customers.
Deep, demonstrable expertise in distributed systems, microservices, and cloud-native SaaS architectures (AWS, GCP, or Azure).
Proven track record working with and through globally distributed engineering teams across multiple time zones.
Experience establishing architecture practices across multi-team engineering orgs (RFCs, ADRs, design reviews).
Has owned and delivered significant technical transformation or modernization inside a matrix organization, with influence rather than direct authority over much of the surface area.
Management experience leading teams of 10–25 people directly, while remaining hands-on and technically current.
Technical Depth
Modern AI architecture. Demonstrated depth designing AI-centric systems that actually shipped in product — not prototypes, pilots or strategy decks.
Generative AI. Deeply conversant and hands-on across the modern GenAI stack: foundation models and model selection, RAG and retrieval architecture, embeddings and vector stores, agentic patterns and tool use, orchestration frameworks, fine-tuning and adaptation, evaluation and guardrails, and latency/quality/cost trade-offs.
Cloud architecture. Expert-level cloud architecture and operations, including infrastructure as code, modern CI/CD and deployment pipelines, containers and orchestration, observability, resilience and multi-region design.
Cost management. Real expertise in the cost side of modern engineering — AI inference and token economics, the cost of AI-assisted development, and cloud operational spend — with a track record of moving unit economics in the right direction.

Experience in B2B SaaS, multi-tenant platforms, or sales enablement / GTM tech.
Background in platform/developer-experience engineering.
Open-source contributions or public technical writing that demonstrates architectural thinking.
Familiarity with security-by-design, SOC 2, and compliance-aware architecture.

s.h: What We're Looking For — Personal Qualities
s.t:
Works seamlessly across Product, Technology and GTM without formal authority, building the trust that makes influence possible.
Constructively collaborative but firm — anchored in a fact-based belief system, willing to hold a position on the evidence and equally willing to change it on better evidence.
Senior-level gravitas and presence, with the judgment and polish to present to the executive leadership team and the board.
Able to express complex technical concepts in a genuinely consumable way, calibrated to the audience — board member, customer executive, product manager or engineer.
Comfortable partnering with a deeply technical CEO and going as far down into the technology underpinnings as the conversation requires.
Why This Role Matters
Two strong companies have become one platform opportunity. The decisions this role makes over the next 24 months — on AI architecture, on modernization sequencing, on how we build and what it costs to run — will shape Showpad's product for the next decade. It is an unusually direct line between architectural craft and company outcome.
